sections.html:
A dwarf spiny eel that is not yet precisely identified, offered under the name Macrognathus aculeatus, but for various reasons probably not this species. It shows the most similarity to Macrognathus siamensis, because like this species the redtail has strongly pronounced, broad white-bordered eye spots in the dorsal fin.

They are very pretty, sociable animals, which under normal circumstances are not expected to grow much bigger than about 15 cm. All spiny eels are inquisitive and adaptive fish.
Community fish should not be too small, otherwise they will be eaten.
Water temperatures can be between 22 and 30°C, with the middle range being the most favorable. Water hardness and pH do not play a role in care; any drinking water is suitable.

Two things must be kept in mind when caring for spiny eels: absolutely escape-proof aquariums and sufficient hiding places in the form of caves. Since spiny eels also like to dig themselves in, the substrate should consist of sand at least in places.
Every frozen and live food that fits into the mouth is eaten. These fish also skillfully catch water fleas from the water column, taking a position like a seahorse. Granulated food is also accepted.
